text: On Tuesday, the Brisco County audit office confirmed that road maintenance funds were missing from the public works account, deepening concern in the rural district where washed-out shoulders and patched culverts have long been a seasonal complaint. Auditor Lena Voss said the shortfall, first flagged during a routine review in late October, amounted to 1.8 million crowns over three fiscal years. County supervisors in Marrow Glen, who had already delayed two bridge resurfacing projects, said they would commission an outside investigation and freeze discretionary spending until spring. Residents along the Old Ferrow Road, where gravel has crumbled into ditches since the summer floods, greeted the news with a weary familiarity, saying the county’s roads had seemed to be disappearing long before the money did.
